DESIGN (notes/design.md): scripted perception, grasp and carry. Learned: 2 alignment steps plus up to 18 descent steps, as bounded residuals in a, b, yaw and step size. AWAC learner using all real data. Limits as the operator asked: 20 N grasp approach, 25 N descent, 65 N session cap. No simulator. SGS-RL was not reviewed or used.

note:
Operator note 17:58 (episodes 0-3 all ended with the drawer's bottom ON the rim: bottom 0.095-0.103 m vs rim 0.095, a
force stop at every downward step, learned x/y corrections within +-5 mm, and "opening not measured (edge not found)"
so alignment used the stored rim). The clearance is only a few mm per side (drawer ~10.5 x ~7 cm vs opening 11.5 x
7.6 cm), so the stored geometry (+-1 cm) is not enough; fix the alignment before the descent, not by pushing:
1. Hold the drawer ~2-3 cm above the rim and take a wrist look-down there: the drawer's bottom edges and the opening's
   inner edges are both visible in one image (the opening's edges are sharp and high-contrast in wrist_opening.jpg);
   measure the offset and yaw error directly (drawer vs opening, same image, no calibration needed) and correct it.
   Repeat once. Fix the opening detector (it failed in all episodes) or detect the wall tops as bright strips.
2. Then descend; on contact, back off 3 mm and make a lateral/yaw search step larger than the clearance error
   (2-4 mm, 1-2 deg), not a sub-mm step. A slight tilt (2-3 deg, leading edge low) to catch one wall first and then
   straighten is the classic peg-in-hole trick.
3. Keep the RL action meaningful: residuals on top of the measured alignment with a range of +-8 mm / +-4 deg.

what: Episode 4 reviewed: alignment now measured drawer-vs-opening in the wrist image above the rim, with a larger contact search (commit 94268dd)
report:
NOT YET VERIFIED: none of this has run on the robot or in a dry run, and its first real use will be the next training episode. That episode also uses a new grasp orientation and new correction moves. The measurement was tested on recorded 640 px wrist video from episodes 2-4, and the motion logic with a fake session plus model checks on the nominal kinematics (this machine has no per-arm fit). No episode has inserted the drawer yet.

Main finding: in one wrist image 2 cm above the rim, the drawer sat 3.3-3.7 mm off the opening along b in all three episodes checked (attempts 16, 18, 20). The clearance along b is about 1 mm per side, so this is the best explanation so far for the jams. My previous correction saw only about half of it.

Done from the operator's 17:58 note (commit 94268dd):
1. Alignment before the descent: 2.5 cm above the rim the program measures the drawer against the opening, corrects, repeats once, and logs what is left in summary.json under `align`. The grasp orientation now keeps the camera on the near-wall side, where both are visible.
2. Search on contact: back off 3 mm, then try a new point around the measured alignment (+-3 mm in a and b, +-1.5 deg), up to 7 contacts.
3. RL action: residuals of +-8 mm and +-4 deg around the measured alignment, and the observation now holds that residual.

Differences from the note:
- Only b is measured drawer-against-cabinet in the same image. The near wall's outer edge moved about 8 mm between episodes because its outer face is in view, so a and yaw still use the rim measured before the grasp.
